name: Spun Wire
description: Each key spins a wheel of six tuned wires past a plucker: slow turns are single plucks, fast ones melt into a sung tone, and a key let go coasts down to a last few notes.

params.name: Tuning
params.description: How the six wires of a key are tuned: all alike, over four octaves, up its overtones to the ninth, or as an open fan of fifths above and below.

params.name: Gesture
params.description: How a key moves its wheel: driven while it is down, thrown once and left to slow, turned once round, or rocked back and forth.

params.name: Plucker
params.description: What the wires are carried past. A feather is soft and round, a card slaps and stops, a nail is bright and thin, and air breathes on them.

params.name: Hub
params.description: What the wires are fixed to. Steel lets them ring and adds metal, wood warms and shortens them, and a skin booms under them and stops them soon.

params.name: Spin
params.description: How many wires pass the plucker each second once the wheel is up to speed. Low counts are notes one by one and high ones run together.

params.name: Melt
params.description: The speed at which plucks melt into a steady rub of the same wires. Below it every pass is heard and well above it none is.

params.name: Spin up
params.description: How long the wheel takes to come up to speed after the key goes down, so the notes start apart and draw together.

params.name: Coast
params.description: How long the wheel takes to come to rest when nothing drives it. The plucks grow softer and further apart until the last.

params.name: Gear
params.description: How the wheels of a chord are joined. At zero each runs free, at one all turn alike, at two and three higher keys are geared faster in whole ratios, and at four slower.

params.name: Wires
params.description: How many of the six wires are strung. One repeats a single wire, and each wire more adds the next note of the tuning.

params.name: Lacing
params.description: How far the wires are tied together at the rim. At zero each speaks alone, and tied fast every pluck ripples on through its neighbours.

params.name: Wobble
params.description: How far the wheel is out of true. Its speed wanders, some wires are touched harder, and the tone swells once in every turn.

params.name: Gauge
params.description: How stiff the wires are. Fine wire sings a clean harmonic note and heavy wire stretches its overtones until it sounds like a bar or a bell.

params.name: Ring
params.description: How long a wire sings after it is touched. Short keeps the passes apart as dry notes, and long blurs them into one another.

params.name: Damp
params.description: How much sooner the high overtones die than the note itself. Low stays glassy, and high leaves a round dark tone.

params.name: Edge
params.description: How sharp the plucker is. A blunt one moves the whole wire softly, and a keen one brings out its top.

params.name: Pluck Point
params.description: Where along the wires they are touched. Near the end is thin and nasal, and the middle is hollow, with every second overtone missing.

params.name: Beat
params.description: How far the wires are tuned off one another, so they beat as they ring together. At zero they are exactly in tune.

params.name: Rim
params.description: How much of the wires is heard through the hub and the rim, and how little straight from the wire.

params.name: Release
params.description: How long the wires ring once the key is let go. Short makes the last plucks of a slowing wheel dry, and long lets them sing into one another.

params.name: Width
params.description: How far the wires travel from side to side as the wheel carries them round, down to mono at zero.

params.name: Volume
params.description: Output level of the instrument. A soft clip after it rounds off the peaks when many keys are held.

origin.note: Written for live-mix on cpp/kit. Six string loops a key, in the extended plucked string form kit/string.h gives, stand on a wheel with a drive, inertia and friction; a wire that passes the plucker takes one impulse at its own place in its period, and as the passes come too fast to be told apart the same impulse, made small, goes in every period instead, so the rub grows out of the plucks with no seam. Simplified: the plucker does not stop the wire it touches, the rim is a loss the wires share, and the hub is six resonances a side. The constants were chosen here and checked by measurement; it is not a model of any one instrument.
